mainTopic: מעילה on every kind of הקדש and its contents, a holy animal's milk, holy produce, and benefit from a הקדש field's dust.
overview: The משנה finishes listing the kinds of הקדש: things fit for the מזבח, for בדק הבית, or for neither. מעילה applies to all of them. It gives five examples: a cistern, a garbage dump, a dovecote, a tree and a field. If they were consecrated while already full, מעילה applies to their contents too. If they were consecrated empty and filled up later, only the item itself is under מעילה. רבי יוסי says that the growths of a consecrated field or tree are also holy. The משנה adds that a baby animal may not nurse from a holy mother, and that workers and work animals may not eat holy produce. The גמרא learns that a holy animal's milk is holy from a בכור, through the words 'passing' and 'its mother.' It learns from 'do not muzzle the ox in its threshing' that the right to eat while working does not apply to הקדש. Finally, threshing one's own קלעילין in a הקדש field is מעילה, because the field's loose dust helps the קלעילין.

steps.title: Every kind of הקדש carries מעילה, even if unusable in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of categories of הקדש and rules that מעילה applies in every one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Something can be fit for the altar] but not for Temple maintenance, or fit for Temple maintenance but not for the altar, or fit for neither the altar nor Temple maintenance. In all these cases, one is liable for misusing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list of the different ways something can be הקדש. It rules that in all of them a person who misuses it violates מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think מעילה only applies to things the Temple can actually use, like an animal for the מזבח or stones for building. The משנה says no: even something useless to the Temple is still holy property, because it can be sold and the money used for the Temple. So the label of הקדש is what counts, not whether the item itself is usable.

keyTerms.meaning: Temple maintenance; the fund for repairing and building the בית המקדש
The altar, where קרבנות are offered
One is liable for מעילה, the sin of misusing holy property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'fit for neither' means it is not הקדש at all. It is still fully הקדש. It just can't be used directly, so its value goes to the Temple.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole משנה: מעילה depends on the item being הקדש, not on how the Temple will use it.

phrases.english: but not for Temple maintenance,
for Temple maintenance but not for the altar,
neither for the altar nor for Temple maintenance –
one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of categories, which began just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעילה applies to all הקדש, whether fit for the מזבח, for בדק הבית, or for neither.

steps.title: The משנה asks for examples
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks 'How so?' to set up concrete examples of each category.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is a setup. The משנה is getting ready to show real examples of the categories it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a request to make the abstract categories concrete. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? A word the משנה uses to bring examples

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for illustrations of the categories stated in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Concrete cases showing each category of הקדש.

steps.title: Five examples: the container and its contents both carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five consecrated items, each 'full' of something, and rules that מעילה applies both to the item and to what is in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one consecrated a cistern full of water, garbage dumps full of manure, a dovecote full of pigeons, a tree full of fruit, or a field full of grass, one is liable for misusing them and what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers 'How so?' with five cases of something that was made הקדש together with its contents. It rules that מעילה applies to both the outside and the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case fits one of the categories. The water in the cistern can be used for Temple building but not for the מזבח. The pigeons and the fruit can go on the מזבח, but the dovecote and the tree can't be used for building. The manure and the grass fit neither, so they get sold for the Temple. In every case, both the item and what fills it are הקדש and carry מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated; made something הקדש
Garbage dumps or dunghills
A dovecote, a house for pigeons
And on what is inside it; the contents

steps.whatToRemember: Everything that is הקדש carries מעילה, even if the Temple can't use it directly. When you consecrate a container that is full, its contents are included too.

phrases.english: If one consecrated a cistern full of water,
garbage dumps full of manure,
a dovecote full of pigeons,
a tree full of fruit,
a field full of grass –
one is liable for misusing them and what is inside them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'כיצד' of step 2 with concrete cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five examples covering the categories, with the ruling that מעילה applies to both the items and their contents.

steps.title: Consecrated empty, filled up later: no מעילה on the contents
steps.stepSummary: If the item was consecrated while empty and only filled up afterward, מעילה applies to the item itself but not to what is inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if someone consecrated an empty cistern, dump, dovecote, tree, or field, and only later it filled with water, manure, pigeons, fruit, or grass, then using the item itself is מעילה, but using what is inside it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the flip side of the last ruling: the same five items, but this time they were consecrated empty and filled up later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the contents were already there at the moment of הקדש, so they became holy too. Here the contents came only after the הקדש, so only the container or land is holy. The key factor is timing: what existed at the moment of consecration.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern or pit for water
A garbage or manure dump
It became filled, later on

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the item stops being הקדש. The cistern or field is fully holy; only the later contents are not covered by מעילה.

phrases.english: But if one consecrated a cistern
and afterward it was filled with water,
a garbage dump, and afterward it was filled with manure,
a dovecote, and afterward it was filled with pigeons,
a tree, and afterward it was filled with fruit,
a field, and afterward it was filled with grass –
one is liable for misusing them,
but one is not liable for misusing what is inside them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם הִקְדִּישׁ בּוֹר וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַלֵּא מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to Step 3: consecrated empty instead of full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contents that came after consecration are not subject to מעילה; the item itself is.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: growth of a consecrated field or tree is also holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that for a field and a tree, מעילה applies to what grows later too, because it grew from הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: if someone consecrates a field or a tree, מעילה applies to them and to what grows on them, because those are growths of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the previous ruling, but only for the field and the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water, manure, and pigeons just come into a container from outside. But grass and fruit actually grow out of the holy land or tree itself. So רבי יוסי treats them as part of the הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Growths, what grows out of something
Growths that came from consecrated property

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between things that merely fill a holy item and things that grow out of it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
One who consecrates the field or the tree –
one is liable for misusing them and their growth,
because they are growths of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes Step 4 for the field and tree cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Growths of a consecrated field or tree are subject to מעילה even if they grew after the consecration.

steps.title: A young animal may not nurse from a holy mother
steps.stepSummary: The offspring of a מעשר animal or a consecrated animal may not nurse from it, though some people make a condition to allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of a tithed animal may not nurse from the tithed mother, and others make a condition to allow this. The offspring of consecrated animals may not nurse from the consecrated animals, and others make a condition to allow this.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a related rule: the milk of a holy animal is holy, so a non-holy baby animal may not drink it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby is not holy, so letting it drink holy milk would be using הקדש for a regular purpose. Some people avoid this problem by stating a condition when they consecrate, so the holiness does not include the milk.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring, a young animal
An animal that became מעשר בהמה, the animal tithe
Consecrated animals, קדשים
It may nurse, suckle
Make a condition this way, to allow it

phrases.english: The offspring of a tithed animal –
phrases.notes: This is a baby born before its mother became tithed, so the baby itself is not holy.

phrases.english: may not nurse from the tithed mother,
and others make a condition this way.
phrases.notes: Some people make a condition that the holiness won't cover the milk, so the baby may nurse.

phrases.english: The offspring of consecrated animals –
may not nurse from the consecrated animals,
and others make a condition this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַד הַמְעוּשֶּׂרֶת לֹא יִנַק מִן הַמְעוּשֶּׂרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from growths of הקדש to another product of הקדש: milk of a holy animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-holy offspring may not nurse from a holy mother unless a condition was made.

steps.title: Workers and work animals may not eat holy produce
steps.stepSummary: Workers handling הקדש produce may not eat consecrated dried figs, and a cow may not eat consecrated vetch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Workers may not eat from consecrated dried figs. And likewise, a cow may not eat from consecrated vetch.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that the usual right of workers to eat while working does not apply to holy produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a worker, and even a work animal, may eat from the produce he is working on. But eating הקדש would be מעילה, so this right does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Hired workers
Dried figs
Vetch, a plant used as animal feed

steps.whatToRemember: Holy property may not be used for ordinary benefit. This covers contents that were there when it was consecrated, milk from holy animals, and produce workers handle. רבי יוסי adds growths of a holy field or tree.

phrases.english: The workers may not eat
from consecrated dried figs.
And likewise, a cow from consecrated vetch.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפּוֹעֲלִים לֹא יֹאכְלוּ מִן גְּרוֹגְרוֹת הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of not letting someone benefit from הקדש: workers and work animals eating holy produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers and work animals may not eat from consecrated produce.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the baby may not nurse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the offspring of a מעשר animal may not nurse from its mother, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה teaches that the baby of a tithed animal may not nurse from the tithed animal. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a line from the משנה and asking for its source. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the baby may not nurse, which means the mother's milk counts as holy. But where does the תורה say that a holy animal's milk is also holy? The גמרא wants a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)
It teaches; used when quoting the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It teaches: the offspring of the tithed animal
may not nurse from the tithed animal.
From where do we know these things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and asks for the source of the nursing rule from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows a holy animal's milk is also holy, so the baby may not nurse from it.

steps.title: The word 'passing' links מעשר to a בכור
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי learns it from the shared word 'passing' in the פסוקים of מעשר and בכור. Just as מעילה applies to the whole בכור, it applies to the milk of a מעשר animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי said: We learn it from the word 'passing' here and 'passing' there, from a בכור. Just as מעילה applies to a בכור, so too מעילה applies to the milk of a tithed animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי בר אמי answers the question. He links the מעשר animal to a בכור through a word that appears in both פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the מעשר פסוק and the בכור פסוק use the idea of 'passing'. This shared word (a גזירה שוה) tells us to treat them alike. Since מעילה applies to all of a בכור, it also applies to every part of a מעשר animal, including its milk. So the baby may not drink it.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned from
'Passing', a word found in the פסוקים of both מעשר and בכור
The firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth
מעילה applies to it, so it is forbidden to use for yourself
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get stuck asking whether a בכור has milk. The point is only that all of a בכור is holy, so all of a מעשר animal is holy too, and that includes its milk.

phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami said:
It is learned from 'passing' and 'passing,' from a firstborn,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:32 for מעשר, and שמות 13:12 for בכור.

phrases.english: just as with a firstborn, מעילה applies to it,
so too the milk of a tithed animal, מעילה applies to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 for the מעשר animal.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'passing' from בכור shows that מעילה applies to a מעשר animal's milk.

steps.title: The words 'its mother' link קדשים to a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The milk of a consecrated animal is also learned from a בכור, through the shared words 'its mother'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The milk of a consecrated animal too is learned from 'its mother' and 'its mother,' from a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by giving a source for the other case in the משנה, a consecrated animal (מוקדש).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'passing' only covered מעשר. For other קדשים, a different shared phrase, 'its mother', links them to a בכור. So their milk is also under מעילה, and the baby may not nurse.

keyTerms.meaning: The milk of a consecrated animal
'Its mother', a word found in the פסוקים of both קדשים and בכור

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases in the משנה come from a בכור: מעשר through 'passing', and קדשים through 'its mother'. Since all of a בכור is under מעילה, so is the milk of these animals.

phrases.english: The milk of a consecrated animal too,
is learned from 'its mother' and 'its mother,' from a firstborn.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27 for קדשים, and שמות 22:29 for בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method as step 9 for the second case in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'its mother' from בכור shows that מעילה applies to a consecrated animal's milk.

steps.title: Why may the cow not eat the הקדש produce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about workers and an animal not eating הקדש produce, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The workers may not eat, etc. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' points to the whole line, including the cow that may not eat הקדש vetch. The answer that follows is about an animal working, so the question is really about the cow.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: The workers may not eat, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' means the rest of that line in the משנה, including the cow that may not eat the הקדש vetch (step 7).

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the source for the rule from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an animal working with הקדש produce may not eat from it.

steps.title: 'Its threshing' means only your own threshing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי reads 'do not muzzle the ox in its threshing' as applying only to your own produce, not to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי said: Because the פסוק says, 'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes.' 'Its threshing' means yours, and not threshing of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי בר אמי gives the reason from a פסוק about not muzzling an ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the תורה forbids muzzling an ox while it works, so it can eat. רב אחדבוי reads 'its threshing' as threshing that belongs to you. When the produce belongs to הקדש, this מצוה does not apply, so the animal may not eat from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not muzzle
Its threshing
Property that belongs to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The מצוה to let a working animal eat only applies to your own produce. With הקדש produce the animal may not eat, because that would be מעילה.

phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami said:
Because the verse says:
'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes,'
'its threshing' means yours,
and not its threshing of הקדש.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'do not muzzle an ox in its threshing' covers only your own produce, so an animal working with הקדש produce may not eat it.

steps.title: Threshing in a הקדש field is מעילה
steps.stepSummary: Someone who threshes his own קלעילין in a הקדש field is guilty of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who threshes קלעילין in a field that belongs to הקדש has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about threshing: if someone threshes his own קלעילין, a kind of legume, in a field owned by הקדש, he is guilty of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קלעילין belong to him. It is the field that belongs to הקדש. So the ruling means he is guilty because of the benefit he gets from using the הקדש field. This ruling sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of legume that gets threshed
A field that belongs to the Temple treasury
He is guilty of מעילה, meaning he improperly benefited from הקדש

phrases.english: One who threshes kalilin
phrases.notes: These are his own legumes, not הקדש. Only the field belongs to הקדש.

phrases.english: in a consecrated field is liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of threshing and הקדש from the 'do not muzzle the ox' discussion, now from the angle of using a הקדש field to thresh.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Threshing one's own קלעילין in a הקדש field makes a person guilty of מעילה.

steps.title: But מעילה needs a detached item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: מעילה applies only to detached items, and a field is attached ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for מעילה we need something that is detached from the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted. A field is the ground itself, and מעילה is supposed to apply only to things that are detached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known principle that מעילה applies to things that are detached, not to land itself. Using a הקדש field to thresh is benefiting from the ground, so it seems there should be no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached from the ground
We require

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the קלעילין, since those are his own. The question is how using a הקדש field can be מעילה when the field is attached ground.

phrases.english: But we require it to be detached!
phrases.notes: He means: for מעילה, the הקדש item you benefit from has to be detached from the ground.

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that threshing in a הקדש field is מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעילה requires a detached item, but a field is attached ground, so the threshing should not be מעילה.

steps.title: רבינא: the field's dust helps the קלעילין
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the loose dust of the field benefits the קלעילין, so he is benefiting from detached הקדש dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Learn from this that the field's dust is good for the קלעילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. He says the ruling itself teaches us that the dust of the field is good for the קלעילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is not guilty for using the attached ground. He is guilty for the loose dust, which is detached and belongs to הקדש. That dust mixes into his קלעילין and improves them, so he benefits from a detached הקדש item and the rule that מעילה needs a detached item is satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, meaning we can conclude from this ruling
Its dust, meaning the loose dust of the field
Is beneficial for it

steps.whatToRemember: Threshing one's own קלעילין in a הקדש field is מעילה. The reason is not the ground itself but the loose, detached dust of הקדש, which benefits the קלעילין.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Conclude from it that its dust is beneficial for it.
phrases.notes: 'Its dust' is the field's loose dust, and 'for it' means for the קלעילין.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a different, detached object is the source of the benefit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The benefit came from the attached field, so there should be no מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The benefit comes from the detached dust of the field, which helps the קלעילין, so there is מעילה.
